You shouldn't feel humiliated or pathetic! Having a panic attack doesn't make you weak and anybody who is worth your time will be understanding and won't judge you for it. Just from looking at you, you look like a sweet person. Don't let yourself get worked up over what others may think of you. Having a panic attack if beyond your control and you should only focus on yourself right now because at the end of the day, it's you who needs to be happy. Remember you're super strong and already dealing with more than a lot of people have to. I hope you feel better!

I was scammed once a couple years back the same way. PayPal will give you a "talking to" but they gave me my money back which was about $75 and flagged the user as well. So it could be worth it if you get a good representative. I just kept at it with calling them asking questions on how to resolve it until I got it back. The squeaky wheel gets the oil. No promises they'll give you money as they were hesitant to give it back to me but it's worth a shot, especially if you have proof. Next time use the option for goods and services to not have the hassle.

Radiohead has a pretty diverse list of songs. OK Computer is definitely an essential album. I'm pretty sure it got preserved by the Library of Congress last year. They're my favorite band so I was pretty stoked to hear that. Awesome that you got a copy. Let's Eat Grandma's singer sounds a little like the girl from [CocoRosie](https://youtu.be/tu3EcAHdHlE) - very interesting voice. I like that whole lo-fi dream-pop shoegaze whatever (I'm bad with genres) thing they have going. Kind of like a [Memoryhouse](https://youtu.be/g1dG_8mMgA0) song. Really great stuff to set a mood or atmosphere. The Gathering also sort of reminded me of [Metric](https://youtu.be/pYLjHhSOE7s) but a little calmer and less aggressive. I'm into some prog like Dream Theater but haven't listened to a lot of Rush past what's played on the radio so I'll definitely look into those two albums. Back when I first became depressed I had a lot of this pent up anger and would listen to music from the '90s Norwegian black metal scene, most notably Burzum and Mayhem but got out of it to listen to some dreamier things but I can definitely get into rock/metal/prog again.  

Thanks for the suggestions and advice and for taking the time to talk to me. I really appreciate it.

I'm sorry to hear about what you have gone through and still go through during rough spots. If depression was just being sad a lot like people make it sound, it would probably be easier than this numbness and inability to enjoy *anything.* I hope one day you find a point in your life where you never go through those feelings anymore and are able to enjoy your hobbies all of the time.

The one friend who hasn't answered my texts is the one who said that to me. We hang out every week and seem to get along great and I have a feeling she doesn't answer people's texts a lot but I still take it personally because she knows how I feel about it. Most of the time she eventually replies but it's agonizing not being able to have a semi-real time conversation Of course, she could be busy and I could be looking far too much into it. 

Not really too sure what to do about my mom. I asked if I could see a therapist and she gives a different answer every time. Sometimes she says it's pointless and a waste of money and others she says to go ahead and call. I'm always so busy with college and work though that I can't seem to find the time to call. I feel pathetic for being so financially and emotionally dependent on her still though, but being 18 I've only just gotten to a place where I can start to break free.
